Problem 253. Position chain from Alder to Dover
Knowledge context.
A map can be modeled with relative positions. When several moves are given, their effects can be combined rather than memorized as a picture.
Given facts.
Quartz is 1 map unit(s) east of Alder; Dover is 1 map unit(s) north of Quartz.
Rules.
Treat east as +x, west as −x, north as +y, and south as −y. Add the moves in order. A fact that does not affect any coordinate is irrelevant.
Task.
Where is Dover relative to Alder? What is the straight grid displacement measured as |x|+|y|?
Step-by-step solution.
1. Start Alder at (0,0). 2. Translate each relation into a coordinate move. 3. Adding the moves gives (1,1). 4. That coordinate is north-east of Alder; the grid displacement is |1|+|1|=2.
Answer.
Dover is north-east of Alder; grid displacement 2 unit(s).
Knowledge takeaway.
Cardinal directions become easier to reason about when they are treated as relations that can be composed.
Formal model.
Grid coordinates; each statement adds a vector; sum the vectors and classify the final coordinate.
